---
title: "FesmData"
subtitle: "Processed datasets for ice-sheet and Earth-system models, on the grids of each model domain"
---

FesmData produces datasets for models, such as topography and region masks, on the
grids of each model domain, from the base grid (0.5–2 km) to 32 km. The
[products](products.qmd) are released on
[GitLab (DKRZ)](https://gitlab.dkrz.de/fesmc/fesmdata-products/-/packages), one package
per domain, dataset and grid, versioned by the release; releases can also be archived
on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/communities/fesmc) with a DOI. The
[datasets](datasets/topo.qmd) pages explain how each is made, and how to produce it
yourself, on other domains or from other sources.

## Getting started

### 1. Get the tool

You need [Julia](https://julialang.org/downloads/) (a recent version; no packages to
install) and a copy of FesmData. All commands are run from its folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData.git
cd FesmData
julia fesmdata.jl help
```

### 2. Choose where the data go

The environment variable `ICE_DATA` sets the folder for the data, e.g. in your
`~/.bashrc`:

```bash
export ICE_DATA=/path/to/ice_data
```

Every file goes to `$ICE_DATA/v2/<Domain>/<GRID>/`: one folder per domain, and in it
one folder per grid with all datasets on that grid. A grid folder thus holds everything
a model needs on that grid, and can be copied as a whole:

```
$ICE_DATA/v2/
  Antarctica/
    ANT-8KM/
      grid_ANT-8KM.txt                 grid description (cdo)
      ANT-8KM_grid.nc                  lon, lat and area of the cells
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc    a product of the dataset Topo
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-Bedmap3.nc
      ...
    ANT-16KM/
  Greenland/
    GRL-4KM/
  ...
```

Domains are named after their folder (Antarctica, Greenland, GreenlandPaleo, North,
Laurentide, Eurasia, ...), grids after their domain and resolution (ANT-8KM,
GRL-500M); a grid name thus also gives its domain. See
[Domains and grids](domains.qmd).

### 3. Find what is there

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl list                     # all records (dataset on a domain)
julia fesmdata.jl list Topo                # the records of a dataset (or of a domain)
julia fesmdata.jl list Antarctica Topo     # one record: its grids and files, their
                                           # sizes, and which are already in $ICE_DATA
julia fesmdata.jl list ANT-8KM             # everything on a grid
```

### 4. Download what you need

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM            # one grid
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM ANT-16KM   # several grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Antarctica Topo         # all grids of a domain
```

`fetch` needs the dataset, and a domain or grids (the arguments can be in any order).
Each file is checked against its checksum. Files already present are kept; a file that
differs (e.g. of an earlier release) stops the download, unless `--overwrite` is given.

### 5. Or mirror everything

To keep a copy of all products on a machine (or of a dataset or a domain):

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl mirror           # everything
julia fesmdata.jl mirror Topo      # one dataset
```

It shows the total size and what is already there, and asks once before downloading.
Run it again after new releases to update the copy: only new files are downloaded
(`--yes` skips the question, e.g. in a job).

### 6. Versions and citation

Each release of a dataset has a version (e.g. Topo 2.0.0, tag `topo-v2.0.0` of
FesmData), shown on the [products](products.qmd) page and by `list`. Every file records
how it was made in its global attributes (`fesmdata_version`, `fesmdata_commit`,
`sources`). Please cite the original datasets (see the page of each dataset), and the
DOI of the release where there is one.

Single files can also be downloaded directly from the [products](products.qmd) page or
from [GitLab](https://gitlab.dkrz.de/fesmc/fesmdata-products/-/packages), without the
tool.
